sourceDesc.p: პერსონები და ადგილები სინური მრავალთავის (864 წ.) ტექსტებში.

person.note: Virgin Mary, Mother of Jesus. Designated Theotokos (God-bearer) by the Council of Ephesus (431). Central figure in Nativity and Dormition homilies.
Archangel Gabriel. Appears in Annunciation (Khareba) homilies as the messenger who announces the Incarnation to Mary.
James the Apostle. Could refer to James son of Zebedee or James the brother of the Lord — context determines which in each text.
3 აგვისტო — სტეფანეს ეძიება; 26 დეკემბერი — სტეფანეს მოწამეობა
David, King of Israel and traditional author of the Psalms. Cited as prophet in patristic homilies as type of Christ.
Solomon, son of David, King of Israel. Traditional author of Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Song of Songs. Cited in patristic homilies as a type of wisdom and as builder of the first Temple.; ბრძენი
Lazarus of Bethany, raised from the dead by Jesus (John 11). Featured in Lazarus Saturday homilies.
Zechariah, father of John the Baptist (Luke 1). Could also refer to Zechariah the prophet (OT) — context determines which.
Joseph son of Jacob (OT), or Joseph the betrothed of Mary (NT). Context determines which in each homily.

bibl.citedRange: 65, 2. ქრისტეს მოწაფის სიმონის შერქმეული სახელია (იგივე პეტრე)

place.note: Jerusalem. Holy city, site of the Crucifixion, Resurrection, and Pentecost. Central toponym in homilies on the Cross, Encaenia, and martyrdom texts.
Bethlehem, birthplace of Jesus. Featured in Nativity homilies.
Caesarea — likely Caesarea Maritima or Caesarea Cappadociae depending on context. Seat of Basil the Great.
Golgotha (Place of the Skull), site of the Crucifixion. Featured in Cross and Passion homilies.
Mount Sinai, where Moses received the Law. Also the location of St. Catherine's Monastery where this manuscript was produced.
River Jordan, site of Jesus's baptism. Featured prominently in Epiphany (Natlisgheba) homilies.
Paradise / Garden of Eden. Theological topos in homilies on salvation, the Fall, and Christ as the new Adam.
